recipes.name: Smoked Pork Butt
ingredients_raw: 2 tablespoons ground New Mexico chile powder

steps.text: If desired, soak the pork butt in a brine solution for at least 4 hours or overnight. There's a recipe for a brine on this site titled 'Basic Brine for Smoking Meat'. You should do this covered and in the refrigerator.

Preheat an outdoor smoker for 200 to 225 degrees F (95 to 110 degrees C). Place a roasting rack in a drip pan. While grill preheats, in a small bowl, combine the brown sugar, chili powder and any additional seasonings to your taste.
Apply this liberally to the meat and rub it in with your fingers.
Place a roasting rack in a drip pan and lay the meat on the rack.
Smoke at 200 to 225°F (95 to 110°C) for 6 to 18 hours, or until internal pork temperature reaches 145°F (63°C).

raw_recipe.headline: Smoked Pork Butt
raw_recipe.description: This smoked pork butt recipe can be done with a brined or unbrined pork butt roast. The pork is tender and smoky — perfect for BBQ pork sandwiches.

review.reviewBody: I have used this recipe 5 or 6 times. I always soak in the brine overnight. Make sure you smoke it long enough. I use about 7-8 lb pork butt and smoke atleast 10 hrs. The first few times the pork was done but didn't pull apart. I started going 10 hours or longer and it just pulls apart. Very tender and flavorful. I use a variation of the rub. Don't forget to rinse the brine off before you put your rub on. Let it sit(rest) 20 minutes once you take it off the smoker. I use mostly hickory to smoke it on a weber grill using the indirect heat method.Put a small pan of water directly over the coals and keep it full. Cook the fat side up,to keep the pork tender. Try this recipe and you will be hooked on pulled pork. A great and inexpensive way to feed a small group for your backyard party.

Third time I've made this recipe in my Bradley smoker. First time, followed as written and it was good. Second time, I brined and made the mistake of smoking whole time and taking the meat out at internal temp of165-ish; flavor was still great but not fall apart great. Combined this recipe with some others and the recommendations and did as follows: 1. brined 12 hours overnight then a cold water rinse and pat dry 2. Spread mustard of your choice all over meat. Doesn't matter what mustard as it's just a binder for the rub and doesn't affect flavor outcome 3. Add generous amount of rub all over the pork butt 4. Wrap in plastic wrap for 12 hours (I did during the day) and then leave out (still wrapped) overnight to room temp. 5. Early in the morning, preheat smoker to 200° 6. Unwrap meat and place in smoker for 4 hours OR until internal temp is 150° 7. Take pork out of smoker and wrap in foil. I poured some apple juice and the drippings from the smoker into the foil on the fat side before wrapping in foil 8. I placed wrapped pork butt into my oven which has a thermometer probe receiver. Cooked another ~7 hours to 195° internal temp 9. Take pork out of oven and leave wrapped. Wrap the foiled meat in a towel and place in a cooler for at least an hour--some folks go a full 4 hours. Unwrap and take pictures for proof of amazingness. Fall off the bone results. Best of the three smoked porked butts so far.

I use my own rub which is salt, pepper, granulated garlic, onion powder and paprika. I do inject apple juice and sugar mixture after brining then use a shaker to apply the rub all over after massaging olive oil on the butt to help it stick. Once it hits about 160f or when the bark is the nice color you’re looking for then I tightly wrap it in foil to finish, 205f internal temp. Too much smoke is bitter.Let it rest for 40 minutes then shred. LoL I guess i just gave you my version.

ABSOLUTELY UNBELIEVEABLE SMOKED BUTT! I USED THE BUTT ROAST WITHOUT THE BONE. USE THE RUB THAT IS RECOMMENDED FOR THIS RECIPE. TALK ABOUT AN EASY AND EXCELLENT RUB! IT ADDED AWESOME FLAVOR TO THE BUTT! YOU GUYS NAILED IT! I HAVE AN ELECTRIC SMOKER AND USED HICKORY CHUNKS AND APPLE WOOD TWIGS FOR A GREAT SMOKE. SMOKE PERMEATES THE MEAT IN THE FIRST 3 HOURS, SO STOKE THE FIRE UP GOOD! I ADDED MORE WOOD AFTER 1/2 HOUR, AND THEN AGAIN AFTER AN HOUR, THEN AGAIN AFTER AN HOUR. I SMOKED THESE BUTTS FOR 6 HOURS, AND FINISHED THEM OFF OF MY WEBER GRILL TO REALLY GET THE BARK FINISHED OFF MORE THAN ANYTHING. TEMPERATURE WAS 175 AFTER THIS 6 HOURS. PULLED APART VERY EASY. IF YOU HAVE NOT TRIED THIS RECIPE, DO YOURSELF A FAVOR AND DO SO! IT IS AWESOME PULLED PORK. I FINISHED MINE OFF WITH SOME BBQ SAUCE I PICKED UP AT THE GROCERY STORE THAT I LIKE "SILVER DOLLAR CITY" OZARK RECIPE. MADE BY "OTTS" IN BRANSON, MISSOURI. ITS GOOD AND THICK AND HAS GREAT FLAVOR!

Excellent recipe. I have made this a few times and I soak mine in basic salt water brown sugar brine for 12-24 hours then rub with a pork rub. I smoke my pork roast or shoulder uncovered for 2-4 hours then rap tight in foil with a small amount of Apple juice for another 12-16. I wait till the temp of the roast is above 185 (I wait till about 200) because then I really does fall right apart.

I smoked a 8.5lb pork shoulder yesterday and it was fantastic! I did use the basic brine instructions and it soaked over night prior to smoking. I did a few deviations from the recipe per the comments of others. One was that I used Big James' Pork Rub (which you can search on here). I smoked for 9hrs maintaining 200-220F, but I did wrap in foil half way through. And finally I cooked it with the fat side up. After 9hrs, I pulled it off and let it rest for 20-30mim. Results: "fall off the bone", juiciest, tastiest pork shoulder I ever had. I served a party of 12 and it was plenty. People raved about it all night. What a great feeling!

Brined 8lb. pork butt overnight. Have smoked before without brine and brining it is the only way to go from now on. So much more moisture. Used a store bought coffee dry rub and smoked with apple chips in a electric smoker for 11 hours @ 225 degrees. It was so moist and delicious that in my opinion it didn't require sauce.

Whoever wrote this article has no clue about smoking a pork shoulder/butt. The internal temp needs to hit 200-203 degrees, NOT 145! 145 degrees is the minimum internal temperature for pork products like chops or tenderloin. 145 degrees will ensure that your pork butt will never shred. Allrecipes, take this recipe down unless you're going to correct it!

Best recipe. Smoke with apple wood! Really really good.

*****Make sure you brine for 12 hours! 
Check out the recipe here "Basic Brine for Smoking Meat" and add 1/4 to 1/2 cup of liquid crab boil to brine recipe. Unbelievable!

Great recipe but if you want the meat to fall apart you need to get the internal temp to at least 180-185 degrees. This is the temperature where the bonds break and the meat will fall apart. Also try using apple juice/cider instead of water for a nice sweet flavor

Problem here is using a gas grill. Adding chips to smoker? No! Use a REAL charcoal / wood cooker and do it right.
Perfect recipe. Followed smoker brine recipe as suggested. It was delicious. Even made Brunswick Stew from the leftovers! Thank you

Smoking to an internal temp of 200-205F will ensure "fall off the bone@ tenderness" - be patient and wait for it, you will be glad. A Boston butt will take 1.5-2 hrs per pound at 225F. Hickory is a natural wood for pork.

Made it for the Super Bowl, had to speed the cooking time due to my lack of being prepared so it didn't pull quite as nice as I wanted (this was my fault, not the recipe). It was delicious and I received tons of compliments, even heard a "best I ever had". I added just a little Cajun seasoning and pork producers seasoning to the rub. Great recipe, great instructions. Thanks.

This is a good smoked pork recipe but you should really change the target internal temperature 145 is not going to be good. It should be at least 180 - 195 to break down all the fat and connective tissue that makes it moist and tender. Obviously if you cook it for 10 hours it should be way past 145 but smoking is about internal temps not time. Thanks.
I like to pull it when done and add just a table spoon or 2 of rub to the meat and mix it up just adds to the level of flavor

was great except the internal temp on pork should be 160 minimum to eat and the pork butts need to reach at least 190 before it renders out enough to pull apart . a temperature of 145 is not sufficient .

I smoked a 9.2lb pork butt shoulder on a charcoal smoker using apple and some cherry. It took 9 hours at 190 degrees and it turned out great. I also used the basic brine recipe and added some extra seasoning to it and let it soak for 24 hours and this really tenderized and added juice to to the meat. The smoker also added a little burned crisp flavor edge that you will not get with a crock pot.
Easy and fast recipe to utilize for any level of smoking experience.
